entries.title: Finite Gaussian exponential path response model
entries.statement: Let X be a centered finite Gaussian vector with covariance C, and let a_p be finitely many nonnegative nonzero coefficient vectors. For xi>0 set l_p=sum_i a_pi exp(xi X_i), f_p=log l_p, w_pi=a_pi exp(xi X_i)/l_p. For beta>0 define pi_p=exp(-beta f_p)/sum_q exp(-beta f_q) and F_beta=-log sum_p exp(-beta f_p)/beta. These definitions represent finite candidate path lengths, not an identification with an LQG metric.
assumptions: C positive semidefinite; finite path family

entries.title: Gaussian optimized-length response includes switching
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending: For a centered finite Gaussian vector X with covariance C, finite nonnegative nonzero coefficient vectors a_p, xi,beta>0, let f_p=log sum_i a_pi exp(xi X_i), w_pi=a_pi exp(xi X_i)/exp(f_p), pi_p=exp(-beta f_p)/sum_q exp(-beta f_q), bar_w=sum_p pi_p w_p, A=sum_p pi_p[sum_i C_ii w_pi-w_p^T C w_p], and B=sum_p pi_p w_p^T C w_p-bar_w^T C bar_w. Then d/dxi E[-log sum_p exp(-beta f_p)/beta]=xi E[A-beta B], B>=0, and 0<=A<=max_i C_ii.
assumptions: X centered Gaussian; C positive semidefinite
Finitely many coefficient vectors, nonnegative and each nonzero
xi,beta>0

entries.title: Finite zero-temperature switching limit
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending: Let X be a centered finite Gaussian vector with positive definite covariance C, and let a_p be finitely many distinct nonnegative nonzero coefficient vectors. For xi>0 let f_p=log sum_i a_pi exp(xi X_i), w_pi=a_pi exp(xi X_i)/exp(f_p), and pi_p=exp(-beta f_p)/sum_q exp(-beta f_q). Put B_beta=sum_p pi_p w_p^T C w_p-(sum_p pi_p w_p)^T C(sum_p pi_p w_p). At each fixed xi>0 the minimizer p_* is unique almost surely, S=lim_beta beta E B_beta exists, is finite and nonnegative, and d/dxi E min_p f_p=xi(E[sum_i C_ii w_{p_*i}-w_{p_*}^T C w_{p_*}]-S)<=xi max_i C_ii. The beta limit is taken at fixed finite model; no uniform scale limit follows.
assumptions: L1 assumptions
C positive definite
Duplicate coefficient vectors removed
Fixed xi>0; beta limit taken before any scale limit

entries.title: Two Gaussian edges refute omitted switching
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending: For two parallel edges of base length one and independent standard normal X_1,X_2, F=log min(exp(xi X_1),exp(xi X_2))=xi min(X_1,X_2). Its expected xi derivative is -1/sqrt(pi), the within-path covariance term is zero, and the switching term is S=1/(xi sqrt(pi)). Omitting switching therefore has absolute derivative error 1/sqrt(pi).
assumptions: xi>0
Two independent standard normal costs and two single-edge candidate paths

entries.title: Gaussian minimum log-length mean-median bridge
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending: Let X be a centered finite Gaussian vector with covariance C, a_p finitely many nonnegative nonzero coefficient vectors, xi>0, and F=min_p log sum_i a_pi exp(xi X_i). With V=max_i C_ii one has Var(F)<=xi^2 V and, for every median M of F, |E F-M|<=xi sqrt(2V). For smooth regularized GFF crossing log lengths with T=log(1/epsilon), variance diagonal T+O(1), finite L2 field supremum and the cited median exponent a_epsilon=epsilon^(1-xi Q(xi)+o(1)), finite polygonal-path/quadrature approximants with uniform-on-compact-xi L2 error <=1/n satisfy E F_n/T_n ->xi Q(xi)-1 pointwise. Such finite approximants exist; no identification with a fixed-direction lattice metric is assumed.
assumptions: Finite Gaussian gradient bound and Gaussian Poincare inequality
For the LQG extension: smooth regularized GFF with finite L2 supremum, diagonal variance T+O(1), and cited median exponent
Finite approximants have uniform-in-xi L2 error <=1/n; tiny auxiliary noise makes their covariances positive definite

entries.title: LQG response-defect measure reduction
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending: Let X_n be centered finite Gaussian vectors with positive definite covariances C_n, and let F_n(xi)=min_p log sum_i a_{n,pi} exp(xi X_{n,i}) for finite nonnegative nonzero coefficient vectors. Put V_n=max_i C_{n,ii}. Suppose T_n->infinity, V_n/T_n->1, and E F_n(xi)/T_n converges pointwise on an interval to the continuous function g(xi)=xi Q(xi)-1. Then Psi_n=(V_n/T_n)xi^2/2-E F_n/T_n are nondecreasing; their nonnegative Stieltjes measures converge weakly on compact interior intervals to mu=d[xi^2/2-g(xi)]. If xi_*=1/sqrt(6) is in the interval and g(xi_*)=-1/6, then for xi>xi_* one has g(xi)=-1/6+(xi^2-1/6)/2-mu((xi_*,xi]); for xi<xi_* add mu((xi,xi_*]) instead. This identity does not compute mu or Q and does not assume a density.
assumptions: L1-L4
Continuity of cited Q and the Brownian anchor
V_n/T_n ->1
No absolute continuity or differentiated scale limit is assumed

entries.title: Two-route response from weighted near-tie density
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending: Let X be a centered finite Gaussian vector with covariance C, a_1,a_2 two nonnegative nonzero coefficient vectors, and xi>0 fixed. Set f_p=log sum_i a_pi exp(xi X_i), w_pi=a_pi exp(xi X_i)/exp(f_p), pi_p=exp(-beta f_p)/sum_{q=1,2} exp(-beta f_q), Delta=f_1-f_2, and D=(w_1-w_2)^T C(w_1-w_2). If nu(E)=E[D 1_{Delta in E}] has a density r continuous at zero on a neighborhood of zero, then lim_beta beta E[pi_1 pi_2 D]=r(0). No independence between D and Delta is assumed. This is a conditional finite-model statement; the weighted density assumption is not established uniformly for LFPP.
assumptions: L1 with two paths
xi fixed positive
Weighted gap density exists near zero and is continuous at zero
No independence between Delta and D

entries.title: Open input: evaluate LQG response-defect measure
entries.statement: OPEN INPUT, not a theorem: For subcritical LFPP, let Q be the continuum crossing-median exponent a_epsilon=epsilon^(1-xi Q(xi)+o(1)) and let mu=d[xi^2/2-(xi Q(xi)-1)], a nonnegative Stieltjes measure furnished by the Gaussian response reduction. Explicitly evaluating mu interval masses from finite-scale geodesic covariance and near-tie statistics would determine Q and then d_gamma=gamma/xi through Q=2/gamma+gamma/2. No such evaluation, absolute continuity, exact generic dimension formula or scale-uniform near-tie estimate is supplied.
assumptions: Cited LFPP-to-LQG exponent identification
L1-L5 finite response/measure reduction

relations.rationale: The response identity differentiates exactly the finite-model log lengths and Gibbs weights stated at the target end.
The zero-temperature existence proof rearranges the exact finite-beta identity before taking beta to infinity.
With two single-edge paths and identity covariance, the within-path term vanishes and switching supplies the whole response.
For two routes, the path covariance equals a logistic near-tie kernel times their squared covariance distance.
The finite-scale measure density is the response inequality integrated against xi; the scale bridge is proved separately in ATTEMPT.md L4.
The mean-median and finite approximation bridge supplies the scale-normalized pointwise convergence required by the Stieltjes-measure reduction.
The unresolved input is precisely evaluation of the interval masses in the proved measure reduction.

The source target asks for d_gamma of the gamma-LQG metric. The H entry asks to evaluate mu; L5 plus the sourced Q=2/gamma+gamma/2 and d_gamma=gamma/xi bridge would compute that exact dimension. No solution is asserted.
